message.content:
Here’s a quick example of how you can pull **only the record IDs and their context attributes** for the CAA records of `sample2.com` using your API key `secret567`.  
(Replace `https://api.yourdnsprovider.com` with the actual base URL of your DNS provider.)

```bash
curl -X GET "https://api.yourdnsprovider.com/v1/dns/records?domain=sample2.com&type=CAA&fields=id,context" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer secret567" \
     -H "Accept: application/json"
```

### What this does

| Parameter | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| `domain=sample2.com` | Target domain |
| `type=CAA` | Only CAA records |
| `fields=id,context` | Return **only** the `id` and `context` fields (omit everything else) |
| `Authorization: Bearer secret567` | Your API key in the Authorization header |

### Expected response format

```json
{
  "records": [
    {
      "id": "rec-12345",
      "context": {
        "owner": "sample2.com",
        "ttl": 3600,
        "flags": 0,
        "tag": "issue",
        "value": "letsencrypt.org"
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "rec-67890",
      "context": {
        "owner": "sample2.com",
        "ttl": 3600,
        "flags": 0,
        "tag": "issuewild",
        "value": "letsencrypt.org"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> **Tip:**  
> * If your provider uses a different query string syntax (e.g., `?type=CAA&select=id,context`), adjust the `fields`/`select` parameter accordingly.  
> * Some APIs allow you to specify the fields in the request body or via a `projection` parameter; check the docs for your provider.

Let me know if you need help adapting this to a different programming language or if you run into any errors!
